How this place works

Simple rules, printed in the open.

1

You buy the maker, not just the piece

Every maker has a story page with work-in-progress photos — the pour mid-swirl, the sign half-painted. People come back when they know whose hands made it.

2

Local pickup on everything

Pickup in the Luck area sits next to shipping on every listing. No paying $12 to ship a cutting board four miles.

3

A “Make me one” button

Every maker takes commissions — your colors, your words, your size. One form, straight to the maker.

4

85% to the maker, in the open

85% to the maker, 15% keeps the lights on. No listing fees, no per-click ads, no games.

Sell at the Table

Run by Eric at EPoBuilds Studios — built for makers, not algorithms.

What makers get

  • Your own shelf and story page — your name on your work, with process photos.
  • 85% of every sale. The other 15% runs the shop. That's the whole fee story.
  • No listing fees, no ads to buy, no competing with factory copies of your own design.
  • Pickup or shipping, your call, per piece — set it when you list.
  • Commission requests routed straight to you, with budget and deadline up front.
  • Help with photos and listings if tech isn't your thing.

Apply for a maker spot

Open decisions

The feature Q&A — these calls shape the next build.

  1. 1
    The name

    “The Maker's Table” is the working name. Keep it, tweak it, or scrap it — the whole brand hangs off this one.

  2. 2
    The split

    This draft runs 85% to the maker / 15% to the house. Is that your number, or do founding makers get a better rate?

  3. 3
    Who ships?

    Makers ship their own pieces, or does everything route through you for one box and one tracking number?

  4. 4
    Pickup point

    Makers' own porches, one set spot in Luck, or scheduled pickup days?

  5. 5
    Who gets the five guest spots?

    Open application, invite-only to start, or first come? Same 15% for guests?

  6. 6
    How does money move?

    Card payments split automatically at sale, or buyers pay and you settle with makers after?
